checkins.note: Captured at seed. IBM Quantum Starling is IBM's stated terminal milestone on a roadmap with earlier named systems (Loon, Kookaburra, Cockatoo) due in the intervening years -- those intermediate milestones are the check-ins to watch for, not just the 2029 date.

sourcing_note: ibm.com and research.ibm.com returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch during capture (2026-08-27), so this entry rests on independent technical reporting (The Quantum Insider) rather than IBM's own primary text. The specific numbers (2029 / 200 logical qubits / 100M operations) are corroborated by multiple independent outlets. Re-fetch ibm.com by hand before this claim resolves.
verbatim: IBM's published quantum roadmap sets 2029 as the delivery date for IBM Quantum Starling, described as capable of running 100 million quantum operations using 200 logical qubits.
headline: IBM will deliver a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer (“Starling”) by 2029, running 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits.
resolution_criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if IBM has, by 31 Dec 2029, publicly demonstrated a machine matching the Starling specification (fault-tolerant, ~200 logical qubits, capable of on the order of 100 million quantum operations) -- an IBM announcement plus independent technical reporting confirming the specification counts. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a materially smaller or delayed system ships under the Starling name. NOT_VERIFIED if no fault-tolerant system in this class has shipped by the deadline plus the 30-day grace period.
